before: Diffusion artwork detection can achieve high predictive accuracy without identifying which visual differences survive benchmark confounds. This study develops a twelve-step explainable visual analytics framework combining mathematical features, grouped evaluation, neighborhood diagnostics and a mandatory control-variable gate. An exhaustive AI-ArtBench audit covers 185,015 files; a balanced cohort contains 45,000 artworks, with a native-$256^2$ Human--Latent Diffusion primary cohort of 30,000 and 6,000 held-out test images. A 104-feature logistic probe attains AUROC 0.9824 and F1 0.9420, outperforming FFT-only features (AUROC 0.6839) but trailing frozen ResNet-50 (0.9999) and DINOv2 (0.9997). The handcrafted AUROC gain over FFT-only is 0.2985. Across 1,040 within-style feature comparisons, 542 satisfy an exploratory statistical rule. However, metadata AUROC 1.0000 exposes origin-aligned JPEG quantization, and verified subject matches are unavailable; consequently no comparison is eligible for confirmatory diffusion-origin attribution. Removing ordinal features reduces AUROC to 0.9080, a decrease of 0.0744, while JPEG-quality-50 recompression reduces it to 0.6819. Linked artwork views, uncertainty summaries and explicit projection fidelity make these associations inspectable. The contribution is a reproducible descriptive atlas and forensic diagnosis of shortcut availability, rather than confirmation of an encoding-independent origin effect.
after: Diffusion-artwork detection can rank benchmark origins accurately without isolating which differences survive source confounds. This study combines named image measurements, grouped evaluation, projection diagnostics and a common-support gate. An exhaustive AI-ArtBench audit covers 185,015 files; a balanced tier contains 45,000 artworks, including a native-$256^2$ Human--Latent Diffusion primary cohort of 30,000 with 6,000 held-out test images. A 104-feature logistic probe attains area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) 0.9824 and F1, the harmonic mean of precision and recall, 0.9420. It trails frozen ResNet-50 (0.9999) and DINOv2 (0.9997), while exceeding the internal fast Fourier transform (FFT)-only comparator by 0.2985 AUROC. Of 1,040 within-style feature comparisons, 542 meet an exploratory statistical rule. Metadata AUROC 1.0000 reveals origin-aligned technical information, but JPEG common support and verified subject matches are absent; no comparison is eligible for confirmatory diffusion-origin attribution. Removing ordinal features reduces AUROC by 0.0744 to 0.9080; JPEG-quality-50 recompression reduces it to 0.6819. Linked artwork views and measured projection fidelity make these associations inspectable. The contribution is a descriptive atlas and a negative validity audit, not confirmation of an encoding-independent origin effect.
reason: T8/T11 define AUROC/F1/FFT, retain numbers, give the negative finding plainly.

Refinements comprise NumPy Lloyd clustering, a combined HSV+Lab family with isolated ablations, whole-source-group randomization and paired fixed-geometry silhouette bootstraps. The released \texttt{manuscript/tables/changes.csv} records their validity costs; none repairs absent controls.
Separate leave-artist, leave-style and unseen-generator experiments were promised but not run. Known artist families are split-disjoint, which does not substitute for those protocols. after:
The plan's four disjoint quadrants remain primary; five overlapping crops add a sensitivity, while the full-canvas comparison also changes dimensionality. The planned development calibration selects $\tau_S=0.01$ from a 0.05 starting cutoff; this is not a fixed-cutoff violation. Combining HSV+Lab changes the primary family definition, so isolated color ablations bound that choice. NumPy Lloyd clustering substitutes for a blocked library implementation; paired silhouette intervals reuse cached geometry rather than recomputing distances.

Separate artist/style/generator holdouts and the GAN arm were not run; source groups and AI-prefix proxies do not establish those generalizations or verified prompts. Missing subjects and JPEG overlap restrict all contrasts to description; whole-group randomization lacks verified exchangeability. The planned movement-by-generator output is a Human--LD style-family heatmap, with resized SD only descriptive. Eight primary cases replace a generator-spanning gallery; semantic/material labels and a user study are unavailable. Dispersion ratios and inter-style centroid distances are cached but omitted from the main results to prioritize control evidence. The released \texttt{results/changes.csv} checks all twelve steps and records these limits and completed stretch analyses.
